_comment: The onboarding path the public preview page answers with: the publisher console's
own four steps, in its order. Your business, Your domain, Your terms, and Connect
your site, whose two tasks are two entries here, done in either order: manifest,
which the preview hands the discovery file on, and edge, which is replaced by the
variant for the detected network. Both are found by those ids. The console reads
only the variants below, for the deploy commands on its last step; the step names
in the wizard's header are its own.
Sources for the commands: the edge worker's deployment instructions for the
Cloudflare path, the CloudFront edge Terraform module for the AWS path, and the
publisher discovery-document reference for the manifest checks.
The integration field on each variant below is the one place that says whether
a network gets a package (edge_package) or a conversation (contact_us). The
preview copies it into cdn.integration; nothing in Go decides it again.
A command marked "checked" is one a signed-in publisher never runs: the console
asks their site the same question and reports the answer. It stays here because
the public preview page has no account and no button, so a visitor reading what
onboarding involves has to see the whole procedure.

Fastly is a conversation, not a package: nothing builds a Fastly package, because the edge build script has presets for the Cloudflare and AWS runtimes only and the Fastly entry point that reads a configuration store belongs to the end-to-end harness. It still has a variant of its own, so a publisher reads that we recognised their network.

steps.title: Your business
steps.summary: The name your payments are made out to. The console asks for it once, before your first domain, and you cannot change it there later. Saving it records you on the Exchange as the party who gets paid. It is the one step you cannot leave for later: the three that follow set up a domain, and you can stop at any of them and finish later.

steps.title: Your domain
steps.summary: Tell us the hostname, and which paths carry licensed content if you license only part of the site. The console works out which CDN serves it, because that decides how the rest of the setup goes. On a network the console can set up, the domain is saved at once and held for you, and it stays Not verified until the last step is done. Nothing changes on your site. Each further domain starts here.

steps.title: Your terms
steps.summary: Choose what an agent may do with your content and what it costs. The terms travel with every offer, so an agent knows the price and the permitted uses before it asks for anything. They are saved when you go on, and they cannot be changed in the console once the domain is verified.

steps.title: Connect your site: serve your discovery file at <host>/.well-known/fora.json
steps.summary: Connect your site has two tasks, done in either order: this file on your site, and the edge package on your CDN. The file tells AI agents and the Exchange who sells access to your pages and who gets paid, and who may add your pages to the catalogue; serving it is also how you prove the domain is yours. Serve it from your own site, as it is: the edge package passes this address through to your site, so your file is the one every agent reads. Edit it later only to change who may sell or import your pages. When the file and the package are both in place, the domain is verified.

commands.label: Check what you are serving
commands.expect: The file below, with "role": "ROLE_PUBLISHER" and your own domain.

steps.title: Connect your site: install the package on your CDN

cloudfront.title: Connect your site: install the package on CloudFront
cloudfront.summary: Your site is served by AWS CloudFront. The package is a Lambda@Edge function for your licensed paths: it lets people and search crawlers through, refuses unlicensed AI agents, and verifies the signed addresses of agents that have paid. Your settings are already inside the zip, so there is nothing to build or configure. Create the function in us-east-1, whatever region your distribution serves from.

commands.label: Create the function from the package
commands.run:
aws lambda create-function \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --function-name fora-edge \
  --runtime nodejs22.x \
  --handler index.handler \
  --zip-file fileb://fora-lambda-edge.zip \
  --role <your-lambda-edge-role-arn>
commands.expect: A function ARN. The role must be one Lambda@Edge can assume, which is the one AWS documents for edge functions.

commands.label: Publish a version
commands.expect: A numbered version. CloudFront associates a version, never $LATEST.

commands.label: Associate it with your cache behaviour
commands.expect: In the CloudFront console, open your distribution, edit the cache behaviour for your licensed paths and add the published version as a viewer-request Lambda@Edge association. Leave the distribution's own signed-address check switched off: the function is what verifies, and both at once would refuse addresses the function had already accepted.

commands.label: Check an agent is refused
commands.expect: 403, with an x-content-rules header pointing at your discovery file.

commands.label: Check a person is not
commands.expect: 200. Ordinary visitors and search crawlers are unaffected.

cloudflare.title: Connect your site: install the package on Cloudflare
cloudflare.summary: Cloudflare serves your domain. The package is a Worker: it lets people and search crawlers through, refuses AI agents without a licence, and serves paid agents a signed address. Keep your DNS records proxied, or requests never reach it.

commands.label: Deploy
commands.run:
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler deploy
commands.expect: You need Node.js 22 or newer. The first command opens your browser once to authorise your Cloudflare account. The second uploads the Worker and attaches it to your route.

commands.label: Check your discovery file is reachable through the package
commands.expect: 200: the package passes the address through to your file, for an AI agent too. A 404 means your site has no file at that address. A 403 means something on your site refuses AI agents at that address; let them read it.

commands.label: Check an agent is refused
commands.expect: 403, with an x-content-rules header pointing at your discovery file.

fastly.title: Connect your site: talk to us about your Fastly setup
fastly.summary: Your site is served by Fastly. We do not hand out a Fastly package yet, so there is nothing for you to deploy today. A publisher can set the package up themselves on Cloudflare and on AWS CloudFront. Adding a network is work we do rather than work you do: the part that runs on your side is small. Tell us about your setup and we will say what is involved.
fastly.note: You will receive the relevant edge package and its deployment instructions when onboarding for Fastly becomes available.

akamai.title: Connect your site: talk to us about your Akamai setup
akamai.summary: Your site is served by Akamai. We do not ship an edge package for Akamai yet, so there is nothing for you to deploy today. A publisher can set the package up themselves on Cloudflare and on AWS CloudFront. Adding a network is work we do rather than work you do: the part that runs on your side is small. Tell us about your setup and we will say what is involved.
akamai.note: You will receive the relevant edge package and its deployment instructions when onboarding for Akamai becomes available.

none.title: Connect your site: talk to us about your setup
none.summary: We could not hand you a package to deploy on <host>. Either we could not tell which content delivery network serves it, or it is one we do not ship a package for yet. A publisher can set the package up themselves on Cloudflare and on AWS CloudFront. That does not mean your site cannot take part: the part that runs on your side is small, and adding a network is work we do rather than work you do. Tell us what serves your site and we will say what is involved.
none.note: This answer is also what you see when a site sits behind something that hides its origin, so it is worth telling us even if you do run one of the two.
